description: Byte-lock for THETA SERIES of Construction-A lattices computed by src/Core/ConstructionATheta.fs. Three lattices are locked: Z^4 and D4 (the external ANCHORS, whose coefficients are published closed forms this repo does not own) and the in-tree E8 (Construction A over AdinkraCode.generator). Integer-only: every value is an exact int64 recorded as BOTH a decimal string and a zero-padded 16-digit big-endian hex string (hex-in-JSON per no-binary-in-proof-lineage; no float ever enters this path). SCOPE: this file locks vector COUNTS BY NORM. That the E8 series equals E_4 evidences that Construction A over the in-tree code produced an even unimodular rank-8 lattice; it is not by itself a construction of a root system or a Weyl group.
generatedBy: src/Core/ConstructionATheta.fs (F# is the generating oracle / treaty)

routeE.how: depth-first enumeration of {x in Z^n : x mod 2 in C}, indexed by the integer squared length x.x, with the exact norm budget |v| <= isqrt(rem)
routeE.reads: the binary code and nothing else

routeC.how: sum over codewords of the product over coordinates of f_p(u) = sum_{m = p mod 2} u^(m^2); exact integer polynomial arithmetic
routeC.reads: the binary code and nothing else - but NO lattice point is enumerated, so there is no enumeration bound to get wrong

anchorZ4.how: r_4(m) = 8 * sum of divisors d of m with 4 not dividing d (Jacobi 1834), evaluated from divisors
anchorZ4.reads: number theory only; an external closed form, not a transcribed sequence

anchorD4.how: the published theta series of the checkerboard lattice D4, transcribed from Conway-Sloane SPLAG ch. 4
anchorD4.reads: an external datum neither route consumed

targetE8.how: E_4 = 1 + 240 * sum sigma_3(n) q^n with sigma_3 summed from divisors (LatticeVoa.sigma3)
targetE8.reads: number theory only; no lattice point is enumerated

enumerationBound: routeE walks coordinate i with a remaining budget rem and admits only |v| <= isqrt(rem). Every later coordinate contributes a NON-NEGATIVE square, so that predicate is NECESSARY for any vector of squared length <= maxNormSq: the walk is exhaustive inside the ball rather than inside a box that happens to contain most of it. Distinct codewords occupy distinct residue classes mod 2, so no vector is reached twice. The claim is nevertheless not taken on trust - routeC has no enumeration bound at all, and an under-enumerating routeE would disagree with it. maxNormSq = 40 for E8 (E_4 exponents 0..10) and 20 for the anchors.
scaling: Construction A gives L_A(C) = {x in Z^n : x mod 2 in C}; the E8 presentation is L_A(C)/sqrt(2). The sqrt(2) is handled by SCALING THE INDEX, never by dividing a coordinate: the scaled norm is (x.x)/2 and the E_4 exponent is (x.x)/4. ConstructionATheta.toShellCounts performs that regrading and THROWS if any occupied index is not congruent to 0 mod 4 - that throw is the double-evenness of the code, checked rather than assumed. Every entry of e8-raw-by-normSq at an index not divisible by 4 is therefore zero, and that is a claim the vector makes, not an artefact of how it was written.
anchors: J. H. Conway & N. J. A. Sloane, Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups - Construction A (ch. 5); theta series and the D4 / Z^n tables (ch. 4)
J.-P. Serre, A Course in Arithmetic ch. VII - E_4 = 1 + 240 sum sigma_3(n) q^n; the space of weight-4 modular forms for SL(2,Z) is one dimensional
C. G. J. Jacobi (1834) - the four-square theorem r_4(m) = 8 sum_{d | m, 4 not| d} d
L. J. Mordell (1938) - E8 is the unique even unimodular lattice of rank 8
S. J. Gates Jr. et al. - the doubly-even self-dual [8,4] code that AdinkraCode pins
no-binary-in-proof-lineage rule; toy-is-free-metered-must-be-earned (this vector is what makes the theta series metered)

series.checkedAgainst: anchorZ4 (Jacobi r_4) and theta_3(q)^4 by convolution

series.lattice: D4 = L_A(even-weight [4,3] code) = {x in Z^4 : sum x_i even}
series.checkedAgainst: anchorD4 (SPLAG transcription) and anchorZ4 restricted to even m
targetE8 (E_4 from divisor sums), routeC, and LatticeVoa.thetaByEnumeration
